s1.syndrome_frame: Keratitis with deep corneal stromal lesions and decreased visual acuity
salient_findings: Brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma
Central infiltrate involving all corneal layers on anterior segment optical coherence tomography
Best-corrected visual acuity of 20/200 in the right eye
key_facts: 68-year-old man with pseudophakic bullous keratopathy
Underwent Descemet Stripping Automated Endothelial Keratoplasty (DSAEK) in the right eye
History of eye infection by Thaumetopoea pityocampa 9 months before DSAEK
Postoperative course was initially uneventful under topical and systemic corticosteroids
Referred for evaluation of keratitis in the right eye two months after DSAEK
Pupils were isocoric and isoreactive without an afferent pupillary defect
No pain with ocular movements
Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showed no conjunctival hyperemia, no discharge, and no epithelial defect
Anterior chamber was deep and clear
Intraocular pressure and fundus examination were normal
Left eye was unremarkable

shortlist.label: Exophiala xenobiotica keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of deep corneal stromal lesions and decreased visual acuity

shortlist.label: Fungal keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Broad category that includes Exophiala xenobiotica and is consistent with the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Acanthamoeba keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of deep corneal stromal lesions, although less likely given the absence of epithelial defect

shortlist.label: Aspergillus keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of fungal keratitis, although the clinical presentation is less typical

shortlist.label: Thaumetopoea pityocampa keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of eye infection by Thaumetopoea pityocampa, although deemed unlikely as the cause of current symptoms

raw.rationale: The presence of brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma and the patient's history of previous eye infection suggest a fungal etiology, and Exophiala xenobiotica is a known cause of fungal keratitis

rejected.label: Fungal keratitis
rejected.why: Too broad, Exophiala xenobiotica keratitis is a more specific diagnosis

rejected.label: Acanthamoeba keratitis
rejected.why: No mention of characteristic ring-shaped infiltrate or history of contact lens use

rejected.label: Aspergillus keratitis
rejected.why: No mention of typical Aspergillus features such as feathery or fluffy infiltrates

rejected.label: Thaumetopoea pityocampa keratitis
rejected.why: Previous infection had resolved prior to DSAEK and is deemed unlikely to be the cause of current symptoms
